title: TCP: Don't use client port for dissector selection
description:
When choosing a payload dissector, don't use the client port. Ie
when the SYN or the SYN/ACK has been seen (and therefor the
client- and server-port are indiscriminitely clear), only use the
server port to search for the appropriate payload dissector.

A bugfix that can be completely disabled and introduces a new preference...? OK, if you say so.

The sole purpose of the configuration option was, that there might be a slight chance, that someone is relying on that functionality not being fixed (they should not, but you never know). commits_data.title: TCP: Don't use client port for dissector selection
commits_data.message:
TCP: Don't use client port for dissector selection

When choosing a payload dissector, don't use the client port. Ie
when the SYN or the SYN/ACK has been seen (and therefor the
client- and server-port are indiscriminitely clear), only use the
server port to search for the appropriate payload dissector.

Some payload dissectors need to be selected based on the client
port instead of the server port. Add a preference to be able to
add these ports. By default Wireshark adds port 20 to the list
to dissect ftp-data for active ftp data transfers, even when the
control channel is missing in the packet capture.
